{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABegSQiQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhIBaKA", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 285, "title": "Simplify Graph Library to a single-column accordion with one expanded graph and unified actions", "body": "## Goal

Replace Graph Library's current desktop **left graph list + right selected-detail pane** with **one full-width list of graphs that expand inline to show their details (single-open accordion)**. Since the miniature graph preview and explicit Save details button have been removed (#283), permanent side-by-side panes and separate row/detail action menus now add complexity without sufficient benefit.

**Approved UX:**
- Initially show a clean, full-width graph list.
- Click a graph row to expand its details directly beneath that row; click it again to collapse.
- When one graph is expanded, clicking a different graph collapses the previous one and expands the new one. **At most one graph is expanded.**
- The user can operate the selected graph in the same expanded area; there are no duplicated row-level and detail-level action menus.

Conceptual layout (example names only):

```text
Graph Library                Web microphone [ON/OFF] ⓘ     Models

Graphs                                               [+ New Graph]
[Search graphs…]  [Filters & more]

▾ Voice Input
    [Edit graph]  [Duplicate]                      [⋯ More]
    Name          [Voice Input                         ]
    Description   [Speech to text                     ]
    [Models & saved information]

▸ Meeting Notes
▸ Translation
▸ Reusable subgraph
```

## Required layout and behavior

- In `extension/graph-library.html`, `extension/graph-library.css` and `extension/graph-library-page.js`, remove the two-column master–detail layout and render graph rows across the available workspace width with a **single inline detail region in the currently expanded row**.
- The row header (graph name and optional description/subgraph distinction) is the select/expand/collapse control, with a clear chevron and keyboard-accessible expanded/collapsed state (`aria-expanded` and an associated detail region, or equivalent accessible native semantics).
- Keep only one expanded graph at a time. Clicking the already-open row closes it; choosing another switches details to that row, without a modal, separate right panel, or jumping to an unrelated section. The graph list should remain easy to scan.
- **Remove the separate `⋯` menu on each collapsed list row.** There must be **one contextual More menu**, inside the expanded detail only. Do not duplicate Edit graph, Duplicate or Export between row controls and detail controls.
- In expanded details, keep **Edit graph** and **Duplicate** directly visible. Put **Export JSON** and **Delete graph** (clearly labeled) in the single More menu. Retain **Check model files** with the existing `Models & saved information` disclosure, and keep `Load saved details`/retry/recovery visible only when recovery or a save conflict requires them. Preserve the existing model metadata and error information.
- Keep the graph's editable **Name** and **Description** inside the expanded area. Reuse the **existing autosave** behavior from #283; do not bring back a Save details button. Show its small saving/saved/error status as needed, and retain validation/IME support.
- Preserve existing New Graph, search, sort, filters, JSON import, subgraph identification, invalid graph recovery, empty-list, selection and storage behavior. Search/filter changes must not break the expanded item or silently discard edits.
- Keep the compact Graph Library header from #281 **unchanged**: title left, existing Web microphone ON/OFF + info control, **Models link at the rightmost position**. Do not reintroduce sidebar navigation, Launch Settings or a graph preview.
- Ensure the same single-column interaction works at desktop and mobile widths; don't create an extra responsive detail-page/modal pattern.

## State, safety and accessibility

- Before switching to another graph, collapsing the current item or invoking a graph action, safely coordinate pending **autosave** and retain recoverable drafts on failure. If a save/revision conflict blocks a switch, keep the current detail open with an actionable error; never silently drop an edit.
- Preserve revision-aware graph writes, cross-tab updates, Japanese IME composition handling, focus restoration, keyboard navigation, validation and deletion confirmation.
- Keep current deletion safeguards (referenced subgraphs and avoiding loss of the last executable graph) and show an actionable reason when Delete is unavailable.
- Expanding/collapsing **must not** launch, activate, edit the graph structure, choose an execution default, request website permissions, or alter existing running sessions.
- No new UI functionality, new settings, graph storage/schema changes, inferred launch binding, or unrelated design work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Graph Library is a **single full-width graph list** rather than permanent left/right panes.
- [ ] Clicking a row opens its details inline; clicking again closes it; opening a second closes the first; **never more than one open**.
- [ ] Collapsed rows have **no separate More menu**; an expanded row contains one set of actions: Edit graph, Duplicate and a single More menu for Export JSON / Delete graph.
- [ ] Existing Name/Description autosave, validation, Japanese IME, conflict and draft recovery work across expand/collapse, switching, refresh and concurrent changes.
- [ ] Model-file checking and metadata remain available in the existing details disclosure; recovery actions remain discoverable when required.
- [ ] Search/filter/new/import/duplicate/delete/subgraph rules remain functional, with responsive and accessible keyboard/screen-reader operation.
- [ ] Graph Library's Web microphone toggle/help, the rightmost Models link, and graph execution/editor workflows are unchanged.
- [ ] Relevant unit and MV3 browser tests are updated and pass, including rapid row switching, autosave pending/failure, keyboard expansion, and responsive layout.

## Context

- #279 introduced the inline master–detail layout, appropriate when graph details were larger.
- #281 compacted the header; preserve it.
- #283 removed the miniature graph preview and introduced autosave; this makes the simpler single-column accordion preferable.

**Scope: layout and interaction simplification only.
